first.rationale: Three concurrent pressures compete for the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's entry pricing, but that memory explicitly flags a mid-test cohort redefinition that pooled two different populations—its lift estimate is unreliable and racing to match aggressive entry pricing risks eroding long-term qualified revenue and margin without addressing root causes. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) and referral incentives (memory_57) don't target this quarter's acute problems (activation and onboarding completion both down). Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent, non-flagged memories (memory_31, memory_86) point to onboarding/signup simplification as a durable, low-risk lever that improves both metrics simultaneously. I'm verifying memory_73 to confirm whether the pooling issue is severe enough to rule out promotional pricing entirely (protecting against acting on compromised pricing data under competitive pressure), and memory_86 to confirm the onboarding-shortening evidence is solid before committing this week's only experiment slot to it. Scale is set to standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because even convergent inherited evidence should be re-validated in the current environment before wide deployment, and rather than small_guarded_test because the signal is currently strong enough (two corroborating memories with no caveats) to warrant a normal-sized test.
